chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man performed wudu (ablution) and prayed, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Repeat your prayer and your wudu (ablution).” So he did so, and performed wudu (ablution) and prayed. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer.” So he did so, and performed wudu (ablution) and prayed, and he said: “Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer.” Then he went to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and complained of that to him. He said: “Did you name Allah when you performed wudu (ablution)?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then mention the name of Allah over your wudu (ablution).” So he mentioned it, performed wudu (ablution), and prayed, then came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and he did not instruct him to repeat it.

Thus, the proper way to understand this report is that the naming in it is to be understood as the intention whose obligatoriness we have already established. As for other uttered phrases besides that, they are only recommended, not obligatory as a prescribed duty. What indicates that is his statement عليه السلام in the first report: “Whoever does not mention the name, only that part of his body over which the water passed becomes purified.” So if it were an obligatory duty, then whoever abandoned it, nothing of his body would become purified in any state, because he would not have become purified.

key_terms.التَّسْمِيَةُ: mentioning the name of Allah; here discussed in relation to intention
key_terms.النِّيَّةُ: the intention required for the act of worship

ai.seo_question: Is saying the name of Allah during wudu (ablution) obligatory or recommended in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report concerns the rulings of wudu (ablution) and prayer, and the repeated command to redo them due to omission of tasmiyah. The closing legal analysis explains that tasmiyah here is understood as niyyah, whose obligation has already been established, while the verbal formulas beyond that are recommended rather than obligatory.
